brief: Morgan Stanley's Mike Wilson, having turned negative on semis in June on extreme earnings-revisions breadth, says the S&P 500 correction (which closed its breadth gap to the average stock to just 2% after Thursday's 4.4% plunge) is entering its final phase: a marginal new low into the 7,100-7,300 support range on lower momentum would complete a classic retest, setting up a year-end rally into 2027, so he recommends adding quality cyclicals and Industrials. The main risk he flags is a Fed that stays more hawkish than expected after the midterms, echoing Powell's hawkish tightening into year-end 2018. That risk showed up a day later: Fed Governor Waller said he leans toward a 25bp December hike with 50bp on the table if core CPI ran hot, and core CPI then came in hot, so a December hike is fully priced with 14% odds of 50bps. The article's own view is that this makes Wilson's risk case (a drawn-out bottom bleeding into December) more likely than his base case, since CTAs are modeled as sellers in every scenario this week.
